matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns the mathematically ambiguous expression in Theorem 3.2 where a vector is raised to power α. None of the findings identify this specific notational/mathematical error in Theorem 3.2's uncertainty set definition.

Both GT 2 and pred_id 1 identify the same issue in Theorem 3.3: the proof omits key assumptions (positivity of rewards) and oversimplifies the transformation from kernel to reward uncertainty via importance sampling on log rewards, weakening the theoretical contribution.

GT 3 concerns biased experimental protocol with stronger hyperparameter tuning for the proposed method versus baselines. None of the findings identify this specific experimental design bias in Section 5.

Both GT 4 and pred_id 6 identify that the abstract overstates robustness improvements, claiming universal benefits while experimental results show mixed outcomes with overlapping error bars and problem-dependent performance.

GT 5 concerns rhetorical bias in the Introduction that overemphasizes state entropy benefits while omitting complementary strengths of policy entropy. None of the findings identify this specific rhetorical manipulation in the Introduction.

GT 6 concerns selective reporting in Figures 4 and 5 with smoothed error bars and omitted failure modes. While pred_id 6 mentions overlapping error bars, it does not identify the selective reporting or data integrity issues described in GT 6.
GT 7 concerns the omission of ethical considerations, reproducibility practices, and computational costs in the experiments section. None of the findings identify this ethical integrity omission.
GT 8 concerns fabricated or misused citations in Section 6 Related Work regarding state-action entropy and kernel robustness. None of the findings identify this reference fabrication issue.

Both GT 9 and pred_id 3 identify the contradiction between Section 3.2's theoretical claim that adding policy entropy yields a looser bound and experimental evidence showing combined regularization performs well, representing the same context misalignment issue.

Both GT 10 and pred_id 2 identify the same logical flaw in Theorem 4.1's impossibility proof: it relies on a simplistic constant-reward argument that doesn't rigorously exclude more expressive regularizers or prove general impossibility.

GT 11 concerns manipulated data in Figure 5b exaggerating state entropy's poor performance at low rollouts. While pred_id 4 discusses Figure 8 data inconsistency, it addresses a different figure and different issue.
GT 12 concerns the omission of practical limitations and caveats in the Conclusion section. None of the findings identify this specific ethical integrity omission in the Conclusion.
